newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Popularity of Brazil's Cardoso remains high - poll.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of Brazil's Cardoso remains high - poll.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's popularity has slipped since December on recent political problems but remains strong because of the economy's stability, a nationwide poll said on Sunday.

The Datafolha survey, published by local daily Folha de S. Paulo, showed 42 percent of Brazilians approved of Cardoso's government, down five percentage points from the 47 percent registered in a similar poll in mid-December.

The paper attributed the decline to several factors, including a mass protest march last month by landless peasants, problems winning Congress' approval on civil service reform and opposition to last week's privatisation of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
The Datafolha poll surveyed 3,811 people in 161 municipalities across the country and had a margin of error of one percentage point.
The poll said 18 percent disapprove of the Cardoso government's performance, up from 12 percent in the prior survey.
"The inelastic way the population evaluates the president could be based on the economic stability," the paper said.
The poll showed 76 percent of Brazilians consider the government's anti-inflation and stabilisation plan "good," while 18 percent said it was "bad."

Folha said Cardoso's approval rating, which began at 70 percent in December 1994, has fluctuated in his nearly two and a half years in office, hitting a low of 30 percent in June 1996 and bouncing back to 47 percent last December.

If elections were held today, however, only 20 percent of Brazilians would vote for Cardoso while 53 percent remain undecided on a candidate, the survey said. No other potential opponent would receive more than seven percent of the vote, it added.
